text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - The Korea Feed Association bought 52,500 tonnes of Argentine corn at $153.50 per tonne on a cost and freight basis on Tuesday. Traders said Andre won the contract with shipment for June 11-30 to Pusan and Ulsan.

- South Korean feed mill companies, including Miwon Co Ltd, Woo Sung Feed Mill Co Ltd and Purina Korea bought 50,000 tonnes of Argentine corn at $154.40 per tonne c&f on Tuesday, traders said. Traders said Toepfer won the contract. Arrival is set for next July 15 at the western port city of Inchon.

BARLEY SALE - The Korea Feed Association Tuesday bought 50,000 tonnes of Canadian feed barley at $141 per tonne, C&F. Traders said Mitsubishi Corp of Japan won the contract with delivery on December 5 to Inchon. KFA had initially invited tenders for 35,000 tonnes of corn and 15,000 tonnes of feed barley. But it decided to buy additional 35,000 tonnes of feed barley as the price was more attractive than corn, they said.

VEGOIL SALE - India's State Trading Corporation bought one parcel of palm olein at its tender on Tuesday, European vegetable oil traders said. The STC bought 6,000 tonnes at $572.40 c and f for October 5-20 shipment from FELDA.

SOYMEAL SALE - Thai feedmillers ordered 36,000 tonnes of 44 percent protein soymeal from Argentina for prompt shipment, sources said. The price was said to be around US$306-305 per tonne C&F Bangkok. The order was placed on September 7. The cargo is expected to arrive in mid-October.

WHEAT TENDER - Morocco will tender on September 18 to import 35,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat for shipment in the first half of October, European grain traders said. Morocco seeks to import 15,000 tonnes of wheat between October 1 and October 10 to Nador and Tangiers and another 20,000 tonnes between October 5 and October 15 to Agadir.

WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC seeks up to 42,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat under the export donation program to Georgia. The shipment period is October 10-November 5 and offers are due by September 23.
- The CCC seeks 25,000 toones of U.S. hard red winter wheatunder the export donation program for Bosnia. Shipment is set for Oct 5-31 and results are due on September 18.

- Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 50,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale. September 17 was set to receive offers. Confirmation would be made on September 18, for Oct 15-Nov 14 shipment.
WHEAT TENDERS - Syria separately offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 was final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.
- The CCC seeks up to 4,410 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soft red winter or soft white wheat for donation to Senegal for October 5-31 and offers are due by Sept 18.
- The CCC seeks 45,000 tonnes U.S. HRW wheat to donation for Ethiopia for November 1-25 and offers due by Sept 19.
CORN TENDER - Jordan is to seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. Number 3 yellow corn for shipment in first half of November. Offers must be received by September 25.
CORN TENDER - CCC seeks up to 4,280 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn to Angola. Shipment is for Oct 5-31 and offers due Sept 18.

- CCC said it is seeking up to 16,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better yellow corn, maximum moisture 14.5 percent under the export donation program to Rwanda. Shipment period is set for December 5-30 and offers are due by September 24.
BARLEY TENDER - Turkey will hold a tender on Thursday to export at least 200,000 tonnes of barley for October-December delivery, a grain official said.

RICE TENDER - The Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan said it had invited fresh bids for the sale and export of 30,000 tonnes of 1995/96 (July-June) basmati rice including seven percent broken. Bids should be submitted by Sunday.
The Republic of the Congo seeks to buy about 13,300 tonnes of U.S. long grain milled rice under the PL-480 Title I and offers are due by Wednesday. Shipment is for Nov 5-20.
SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The Republic of the Congo seeks to buy 3,400 tonnes of PL-480 tonnes of soybean oil. Offers are due by Wednesday. Shipment is for November 5-20.

MARKET TALK - Export traders said they could not confirm market rumors that China is seeking or has bought U.S. soybeans this week, but they said they expect such transactions to occur soon as harvest pressures prices. A rumor that China was seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans circulated at the Chicago Board of Trade Tuesday morning. "I would not be surprised for China to seek this amount since we are looking at them to import 1.5 million tonnes soybeans," one senior U.S. exporter said.

... South Korean feed millers are expected to buy substantially more Canadian feed wheat for shipment from March, 1997 if prices continue falling to levels close to those of imported corn, traders said on Tuesday.
